finding.title: Correct FirestoreCodec.encodeDateTime's false claim that the Firestore SDK auto-converts ISO-8601 strings to Timestamp
finding.rule: AG-8-adjacent doc/code truth + Evans (one place for an invariant)

evidence.quote: The Firestore SDK converts ISO-8601 strings into Timestamp objects on write, so this format is safe to use in push documents.
in Firestore Security Rules a `string <= timestamp` comparison is `false`, which would deny EVERY completion create.
timestamp), so a `created_at <= request.time` guard compared a string to request.time and was rejected at the type level —

finding.why: The claim is false — the SDK does not auto-convert a Dart String to a Timestamp. That's exactly why firestore_gateway_impl.dart carries a dedicated `_timestampifyCompletedAt` patch (lines 158-219) that rewrites `completed_at`/`purged_at` from String/DateTime to a real Timestamp AFTER every codec's encode() output runs, and exactly why streak_events' equivalent `created_at <= request.time` rule check was deleted after it denied every write in production. The real fix for a timestamp-compared field lives two layers away from the codec, in a hand-maintained per-field allowlist inside firestore_gateway_impl.dart — a mechanism entity_codec.dart's own 'Responsibilities' docstring never mentions. The next engineer who adds a new entity kind with a `<= request.time` rule, trusts this codec's comment, and skips the gateway patch will reproduce the exact 'permission-denied on every create' incident this codebase has already hit twice (completions, streak_events).
finding.recommendation: Fix the doc comment to state the SDK does NOT auto-convert and cross-reference firestore_gateway_impl.dart's `_timestampifyCompletedAt` as the actual mechanism. Consider moving that per-field patch logic into the codec/EntityCodec layer (or documenting it explicitly in entity_codec.dart's 'Push encoding — SyncWriteFacade territory' note) so the full push contract for a timestamp-compared field lives in one discoverable place instead of three.
acceptance_criteria: encodeDateTime's doc comment no longer claims SDK auto-conversion; it states the true behavior and points to the gateway patch.
A note is added (in entity_merger.dart's 'adding a new entity kind' checklist, or equivalent) that a request.time-compared field needs a gateway-side Timestamp conversion, not just a codec change.

finding.title: Wrap the DB write in StudyDayConfigScreen._toggleDay with catch/log and a consistent mounted guard
finding.why: _toggleDay runs its DB lookup + db.studyDayConfigDao.upsertDayConfig(...) inside a detached `.then()` async closure with no surrounding try/catch and no caller awaiting the result — if upsertDayConfig throws (constraint violation, disk error), the failure is silently swallowed by the Future machinery with no AppLogger call and no user feedback (unlike the sync-push call three lines later, which IS wrapped in `on TutorWriteException catch`). The same closure calls `ref.invalidate(allDailyTasksProvider)` at line 288 with no `context.mounted` check, yet the SAME method DOES check `context.mounted` before the SnackBar at line 299 just after — an inconsistent, incomplete guard that leaves the earlier call exposed to a disposed-widget race if the user navigates away quickly after tapping a day toggle.
finding.recommendation: Wrap the DB write in try/catch with an AppLogger.error call and user-facing feedback on failure; check `context.mounted` (or equivalent) before the `ref.invalidate` call, matching the guard already present for the SnackBar.
acceptance_criteria: A thrown exception from upsertDayConfig is logged via AppLogger and does not vanish silently.
ref.invalidate(allDailyTasksProvider) is only called when the widget is still mounted.

finding.title: Move ProfileSwitcherBar out of app/router/app_shell.dart to restore AG-5 test mirroring
finding.why: profile_switcher_bar_badge_test.dart sits at the AG-5-mirrored path test/features/profiles/presentation/widgets/, but the widget it tests is defined in lib/app/router/app_shell.dart (a named churn hotspot) rather than lib/features/profiles/presentation/widgets/ — so there is no lib file this test actually mirrors. ProfileSwitcherBar only reads profile/tutoring providers (parentPinAuthenticatedProfileIdProvider, activeProfileIdProvider, profileListStreamProvider, activeTutoredProfileSelectionProvider) and has no router-scaffolding responsibility of its own; it reads as profiles-feature presentation code that landed in the shell file by accretion.
finding.recommendation: Move the ProfileSwitcherBar class into lib/features/profiles/presentation/widgets/profile_switcher_bar.dart (app_shell.dart keeps a plain usage/import), and the test file already sits at the correctly-mirrored path once the source moves.
acceptance_criteria: lib/features/profiles/presentation/widgets/profile_switcher_bar.dart exists and profile_switcher_bar_badge_test.dart's sole lib-under-test import points there, restoring AG-5 mirroring

finding.title: Delete the dead duplicate syncStatusStreamProvider/syncStatusProvider in features/sync/presentation/providers/sync_providers.dart and fix the false 'delegates here' comment in sync_status_providers.dart
finding.rule: AG-4 duplicate top-level symbol names / dead code

evidence.quote:
UI can watch this directly; [syncStatusProvider] in sync_providers.dart
/// also delegates here.

finding.why: sync_status_providers.dart:17-19 and :34-36 both assert that sync_providers.dart's syncStatusProvider 'delegates here.' It doesn't: sync_providers.dart independently re-declares both syncStatusStreamProvider and syncStatusProvider with character-for-character identical bodies (same orchestrator watch, same late-subscriber loading-state workaround, same error mapping), under the same names. Grepping every consumer of these two symbol names across lib/ shows dashboard_screen.dart, backup_sync_section.dart and sync_status_indicator.dart all import exclusively from core/sync/providers/sync_status_providers.dart; nothing anywhere imports or references the copy in sync_providers.dart. It is fully dead code with a misleading doc comment, and it demonstrates the exact shotgun-surgery risk duplication creates: the 'late subscriber to a broadcast stream' loading-state fix (the loop-iter2/orchestrator.currentStatus fallback) had to be applied to both copies in parallel, and nothing prevents the next fix from being applied to only one.
finding.recommendation: Delete syncStatusStreamProvider/syncStatusProvider from features/sync/presentation/providers/sync_providers.dart (confirmed zero production consumers); any future consumer should import core/sync/providers/sync_status_providers.dart directly. Correct or remove the 'also delegates here' comment once the duplicate is gone.
acceptance_criteria: features/sync/presentation/providers/sync_providers.dart no longer defines syncStatusStreamProvider or syncStatusProvider.
grep -rn 'final syncStatusStreamProvider\|final syncStatusProvider' lib/ returns exactly one definition site each.
flutter analyze and the existing sync-status widget tests (sync_status_indicator_l1_test.dart, backup_sync_section_l1_test.dart, sync_status_provider_loading_state_test.dart) still pass unchanged.

finding.title: Split point_config_screen.dart and reward_configuration_screen.dart (and trim 3 more) below the 400-line hand-written file cap
finding.rule: AG-3 (hand-written Dart files <= 400 lines; generated exempt)
finding.why: point_config_screen.dart and reward_configuration_screen.dart are each ~2x the cap: both conflate a data-fetching FutureProvider, a stateful screen with pending-edit tracking, AND 5+ private presentational widgets (_HeroHeader, _CurriculumPointsCard, _StepperControl, _RoundStepButton, _SaveBar in point_config_screen.dart; _RewardPreview, _InlineRewardsSection in reward_configuration_screen.dart) all in one file -- unlike gamification_screen.dart in the same feature, which correctly extracts its presentational pieces into presentation/widgets/ files. This makes the private widgets unreusable and untestable in isolation, and any single-line style tweak risks an unrelated diff touching 700+ lines of unrelated screen logic.
finding.recommendation: Extract each private widget class into its own file under presentation/widgets/, matching the pattern gamification_screen.dart already follows; the 3 smaller overages (403-414 lines) likely just need trimming of inline widget trees into extracted sub-widgets.
acceptance_criteria: wc -l on every hand-written .dart file in features/gamification/ reports <= 400
AG-3's line-count checker (once added to make audit) reports zero violators in this feature
